hints: Draw the prices as a line chart. A long climb from day 2 to day 5 earns the same as climbing each single day along the way. What about the days when the price goes down?
Either keep two states per day (holding a share vs. not holding), or notice that the best plan simply collects every positive day-to-day increase — a greedy sum.

1. Set profit = 0.
  2. For every day i from 1 to n-1:
  3. if prices[i] > prices[i-1], add prices[i] - prices[i-1] to profit.
  4. Return profit.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Recursively try buy / sell / wait on every day.

approaches.name: State DP
approaches.idea: Track free and hold: free = max(free, hold + p), hold = max(hold, free - p).

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Greedy: sum every positive daily increase.

explain: For [4, 1, 6, 2, 5, 7] the rises are 1→6 (+5), 2→5 (+3) and 5→7 (+2), total 10. Summing every upswing is exactly the same as buying at each valley and selling at each peak, and since there is no limit or fee, no trade plan can beat collecting every rise. A falling-only list like [9, 6, 3] never adds anything, so the answer is 0 (just don't trade).
recognize: 'Unlimited buy/sell, one share at a time, no fee' → state DP that reduces to summing every positive price change.
